target: The citation guard's source corpus: it reads this repository's tracked files, and refuses the nested checkouts and vendored trees that a directory walk hands it
note: The review blocker on PR 28 was that the fix had no regression proving the thing it fixed. The planted-citation probes proved `_CITATION` still recognises a bad section -- which the replaced implementation also did, and which an empty corpus would not disturb. These mutations attack the corpus rule itself. Run with: uv run python tools/mutate.py benchmarks/mutations/citation-corpus.json

mutations.name: the-corpus-goes-back-to-walking-everything
mutations.anchor:
where = ROOT if root is None else root
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "*.py", "*.md"],
                         cwd=where, capture_output=True, check=True)
    return [where / name for name in out.stdout.decode("utf-8").splitlines() if name]
mutations.why: the defect as it shipped, restored exactly. A walk filtered only on `parts[0]` lets `.venv312` through and every nested worktree under `.slim/` and `.claude/`, so a citation written in ANOTHER checkout of this repository -- possibly at a commit where the section still existed -- is validated against this tree's ARCHITECTURE.md and blamed on this tree. It also cost 58 945 paths walked to read 265, which is what breached the 5 s L0 ceiling at 19.4 s and had been failing about one run in five before that

mutations.name: the-corpus-is-empty-and-therefore-clean
mutations.anchor: return [where / name for name in out.stdout.decode("utf-8").splitlines() if name]
mutations.why: the failure that reads as success. A guard over no files finds no offenders and is indistinguishable on the console from a repository with nothing wrong in it. The planted-citation probes that preceded this regression would have caught this one and nothing else, which is why the regression asserts a bad citation IS found as well as asserting the nested one is not -- one assertion without the other proves the corpus is small, not that it is right

mutations.name: the-nested-checkout-is-read-after-all
mutations.why: the corpus rule bypassed at the point of use rather than at its definition. A correct `_tracked_sources` is worth nothing if the caller reaches past it, and this is the shape that survives a review of the helper alone -- the helper stays right and the guard still reads somebody else's repository
